statusLevels.live_proven: A user-run in-game test showed the intended effect; the acknowledgement requirement is removed for exactly the family scope.
statusLevels.not_tested: The write applied cleanly in game but the effect was not observed; stays offline-proven with its acknowledgement.
statusLevels.inconclusive: The write applied cleanly but the observation cannot confirm or refute the effect; stays offline-proven, acknowledgement required.
statusLevels.live_failed: A user-run test applied the write cleanly but the intended effect did not occur. The capability is withdrawn for exactly that scope (read-only, with the reason) until the cause is corrected and re-tested.
statusLevels.pending: Not yet shown in game: built for a live test that has not run, or run only against a source later found not to be consumed. Writes keep their acknowledgements.
statusLevels.live_partial: A user-run test showed the write consumed in play, but part of the intended effect did not hold (a separate limit or state caps it). The capability keeps its acknowledgement; the observation is recorded as reported and its cause is investigated before any semantics change.

evidenceModel.donorOutputWorks: the donor projectile or output renders and functions when some host fires it
evidenceModel.referenceWriteSucceeded: Runtime resolved the target and the guarded write applied (APPLIED in the log)
evidenceModel.hostReadsReference: the host's live firing path consumes the member that was written
evidenceModel.gameplayOutputChanged: the host visibly fired the new output in play
evidenceModel.note: A failed host is host-path evidence, never evidence against the donor output. null means the test did not establish that part.

sessions.runtime: HD2Runtime 0.27.0 coverage test build (commit c99d338, build/test-artifacts/coverage-build)

tests.observation: The AC-8 turns dramatically faster; the difference is very obvious in gameplay.
The MG-43 ignores enemies at normal sentry distances and begins targeting only when they are very close.

The launcher deployed mines into only one portion (quadrant) of its normal 360-degree pattern instead of distributing fewer mines evenly around the circle. Reducing the salvo count truncates the normal angular deployment sequence: successive salvos cover different rotational sectors.
Liberator bullets set enemies on fire; the ballistic attack otherwise behaved normally.

Maxigun bullets stun enemies. The observed stun lasted about 1-2 s rather than the catalogued 3 s of Stun Medium. The cause is not established; see research/status-susceptibility-F5FEE03DCFDB.json. Status duration semantics are unchanged.
Normal Chargers became extremely easy to kill with ordinary weapons; Charger Behemoths stayed tanky, so the write reached the intended class only.
Liberator and Stalwart light-penetration shots damaged the Charger's head instead of bouncing; other armored areas still behaved armored.
Applied cleanly, but the Spewer artillery attack could not be reliably provoked in play.
Fabricators tested appeared to need roughly the usual number of Railgun shots. Only one of five fabricator variants was edited and the variant cannot be identified in game, so this is not a failure.

tests.observation: The impact effect worked while the minigun fired its own bullet (projectile Vanilla). With a donor projectile selected the effect did not follow it: the minigun then fires the donor's row, and this write edits the Patriot bullet row (ProjectileSettings row 148) only. That is the API as designed (a slot write edits a row, not a host; docs/attack-outputs.md, host swaps and slot writes), so swap plus effect on the donor is not proven. The row's other consumers (the Gatling and machine-gun sentries) were not reported.
Re-confirmed: the EXO-45 Patriot minigun fired the LAS-58 Talon projectile.

With the Patriot minigun swapped to the LAS-58 Talon output (a separate operation), the grenade-blast impact explosion written directly to the LAS-58 Talon row reached the minigun: its Talon bolts exploded where they hit. The explicit donor-row composition. The LAS-58 Talon sidearm, which fires the same row, was not reported.
